claims.text: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 is an equiatomic refractory-metal high-entropy alloy composition.
Refractory-metal high-entropy alloys containing elements such as W, Mo, Ta, and Nb are of interest for high-temperature applications.
The proposed initial high-entropy nanoalloy has a uniform single-phase BCC microstructure.
The proposed initial alloy has nanoscale grain features.
High configurational entropy arising from multielement mixing creates significant local lattice distortions.
The local lattice distortions act as barriers to atomic diffusion.
Nanoscale grain boundaries impede conventional diffusion pathways in these alloys.
Entropy-associated lattice distortions increase the activation energy for atomic diffusion.
Reduced atomic mobility suppresses the rearrangements responsible for phase separation and chemical decomposition during high-temperature exposure.
Compared with a compositionally similar low-entropy nanoalloy, the high-entropy nanoalloy will retain a more uniform, single-phase structure after annealing.
The high-entropy nanoalloy will undergo less subgrain or grain coarsening than the low-entropy baseline.
The high-entropy nanoalloy will exhibit less phase segregation and greater chemical homogeneity than the low-entropy baseline.
A low-entropy alloy with one dominant element is expected to have greater atomic diffusion and a greater propensity for phase segregation or chemical decomposition under identical thermal conditions.
Composition and annealing temperature can govern phase stability and the length scale of phase decomposition in high-entropy alloys.
Processing history, including grain size and prior thermal treatment, can influence the magnitude of the proposed stability effect.
Nano-precipitation may compete with the proposed entropy–distortion stabilization mechanism in some compositions.
The prediction is explicitly restricted to inert-atmosphere exposures at approximately 800–1100 °C for no more than about 200 hours.
Similar or greater segregation, coarsening, or chemical inhomogeneity in the high-entropy alloy relative to the low-entropy control would falsify the proposed dominant stabilization mechanism.
